questions.stem: For the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) with ΔH = -92 kJ/mol, what happens to the position of equilibrium when the temperature is increased?

options.text: It shifts to the right, producing more ammonia
It shifts to the left, producing less ammonia
It remains unchanged because temperature does not affect equilibrium
It shifts to the right because the reaction speeds up

questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH = -92 kJ/mol). According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature causes the system to oppose the change by shifting in the endothermic direction, which is the reverse reaction. This produces less ammonia (shifts left).
